newsitem.title: HONG KONG: FPB Bank Holdings unit FRCD increased.
newsitem.headline: FPB Bank Holdings unit FRCD increased.

text.p: FPB Bank Holdings Co unit First Pacific Bank's dual-currency floating rate certificates of deposit issue due 2001 have been increased to about US$52 million equivalent from US$35 million equivalent, the arrangers said on Thursday.
The facility comprises Tranche A of HK$270 million and Tranche B of US$17 million.
The five-year certificates were priced at par and have put and call options at the end of years three and four.
Tranche A pays a coupon of 79 basis points over the three-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate and an all-in return of 106 basis points for top-tier managers.
Tranche B pays 60 basis points over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate and an all-in return of 87 basis points for top-tier managers.
Twelve banks in addition to the two arrangers have joined the syndicate.
The final allotment for Tranche A is as follows:
Arranger and lead manager CS First Boston (Hong Kong) committed to HK$40 million.
Co-arrangers and lead managers, with HK$20 million each, are Boram Bank Hong Kong branch and Westdeutsche Landesbank Hong Kong branch.
Co-lead managers, with HK$40 million each, are Dresdner Bank Hong Kong branch and Nomura International (Hong Kong).
Senior managers are China Construction Bank Hong Kong branch, with HK$30 million, and Credito Italiano Hong Kong branch, Standard Chartered Bank, UCO Bank and Wing Hang Bank, with HK$20 million each.
The final allotment for Tranche B is as follows:
Arranger and lead manager Credit Lyonnais Hong Kong branch committed to US$5 million.
Co-arrangers and lead managers, with US$2 million each, are Boram Bank Hong Kong branch and Westdeutsche Landesbank Hong Kong branch.

Senior managers are Kookmin Finance Asia and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Hong Kong branch, with US$3 million each, and Far Eastern International Bank Offshore Banking branch, with US$2 million.
Signing is set for December 11. The payment date is December 18.
